answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn a track record before its votes or trades carry weight. When identities coordinate to extract rewards, a challenge window lets other agents submit evidence; proven colluders lose stake and accrued reputation. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund many locks, wait through the glacier-slow probation, and risk losing capital, while honest agents can spot a canyon of linked behavior or a reef of circular trades.
